chapters.title: Capítulo 1: A pipa na árvore
chapters.synopsis: A pipa de Lelé fica presa na árvore, e os amigos se juntam, um de cada vez, até conseguirem tirá-la.
chapters.text:
Lelé, a lebre, tinha uma pipa vermelha. Ela correu pelo campo e a pipa subiu, subiu, subiu.
De repente, o vento soprou forte, e a pipa ficou presa no galho da árvore.
Lelé puxou a linha. Puxa, puxa, e nada de sair!
Lelé chamou o tatu Tico. Tico segurou Lelé, Lelé puxou a linha. Puxa, puxa, e nada de sair!
Tico chamou a pata Quinha. Quinha segurou Tico, Tico segurou Lelé, Lelé puxou a linha. Puxa, puxa, e nada de sair!
Quinha chamou a formiga Fifi. Fifi era pequenininha, mas segurou Quinha com força. Quinha segurou Tico, Tico segurou Lelé, Lelé puxou a linha.
Puxa, puxa... e a pipa soltou do galho!
Todos caíram sentados na grama e riram muito.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — gritaram os quatro amigos.
E a pipa vermelha voltou a voar no céu azul.

chapters.title: Capítulo 2: A bola no buraco
chapters.synopsis: A bola de Tico cai num buraco fundo, e os amigos formam uma fila para alcançá-la.
chapters.text:
Tico, o tatu, jogava bola com os amigos. Ele chutou forte, e a bola rolou, rolou, e caiu num buraco fundo.
Tico esticou o braço. Estica, estica, e nada de alcançar!
Tico chamou a pata Quinha. Quinha segurou o rabo de Tico, e Tico esticou o braço mais fundo. Estica, estica, e nada de alcançar!
Quinha chamou a lebre Lelé. Lelé segurou Quinha, Quinha segurou Tico, e Tico esticou o braço. Estica, estica, e nada de alcançar!
Lelé chamou a formiga Fifi. Fifi segurou a orelha de Lelé. Lelé segurou Quinha, Quinha segurou Tico, e Tico esticou o braço até o fundo.
Estica, estica... e Tico pegou a bola!
Os amigos puxaram Tico para fora do buraco, todo sujo de terra.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — disseram, rindo.
Depois, eles taparam o buraco com folhas e terra, para nenhuma bola cair lá de novo.

chapters.title: Capítulo 3: A porta emperrada
chapters.synopsis: A porta da casa de Quinha emperra com a chuva, e os amigos empurram juntos até ela abrir.
chapters.text:
Choveu muito na floresta. A porta de madeira da casa de Quinha, a pata, inchou com a água e emperrou.
Quinha empurrou a porta. Empurra, empurra, e nada de abrir!
Quinha chamou Lelé, a lebre. Lelé empurrou Quinha, Quinha empurrou a porta. Empurra, empurra, e nada de abrir!
Lelé chamou Tico, o tatu. Tico empurrou Lelé, Lelé empurrou Quinha, Quinha empurrou a porta. Empurra, empurra, e nada de abrir!
Tico chamou Fifi, a formiga. Fifi chamou mais dez formigas! Todas empurraram Tico. Tico empurrou Lelé, Lelé empurrou Quinha, Quinha empurrou a porta.
Empurra, empurra... e a porta abriu!
Todos entraram rolando na sala, uns por cima dos outros.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — gritaram.
Quinha fez um chá quentinho para todo mundo. Lá fora, a chuva continuava, mas dentro de casa estava seco e alegre.

chapters.title: Capítulo 4: A melancia pesada
chapters.synopsis: Os amigos encontram uma melancia enorme e precisam levá-la juntos para o piquenique.
chapters.text:
Era dia de piquenique. Lelé, a lebre, achou uma melancia enorme na horta.
Lelé tentou levantar a melancia. Levanta, levanta, e nada de subir!
Lelé chamou Tico, o tatu. Tico segurou de um lado, Lelé segurou do outro. Levanta, levanta, e nada de subir!
Tico chamou Quinha, a pata. Quinha segurou por baixo, Tico de um lado, Lelé do outro. Levanta, levanta, e nada de subir!
Quinha chamou Fifi, a formiga. Fifi subiu em cima da melancia e gritou bem alto:
— Um, dois, três... JÁ!
Todos levantaram ao mesmo tempo. Levanta, levanta... e a melancia subiu!
Eles levaram a melancia até a sombra da árvore, devagarinho, passo a passo.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — disseram, cansados e felizes.
Quinha cortou a melancia em fatias. Cada amigo ganhou um pedaço vermelho e doce. E Fifi ganhou a primeira fatia, porque foi ela quem contou até três.

chapters.title: Capítulo 5: O barquinho encalhado
chapters.synopsis: O barquinho de Quinha fica preso na areia do rio, e os amigos o empurram de volta para a água.
chapters.text:
Quinha, a pata, tinha um barquinho de madeira. Um dia, o barquinho ficou preso na areia, na beira do rio.
Quinha empurrou o barquinho. Empurra, empurra, e nada de boiar!
Quinha chamou Fifi, a formiga. Fifi empurrou junto com Quinha. Empurra, empurra, e nada de boiar!
Fifi chamou Tico, o tatu. Tico cavou a areia em volta do barquinho, e todos empurraram. Empurra, empurra, e nada de boiar!
Tico chamou Lelé, a lebre. Lelé teve uma ideia:
— Vamos esperar a água subir um pouquinho e empurrar todos juntos!
Os amigos esperaram. Quando a água chegou mais perto, todos empurraram ao mesmo tempo.
Empurra, empurra... e o barquinho boiou!
Quinha subiu no barco e chamou os amigos.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — cantaram todos.
E os quatro passearam pelo rio até o sol se pôr.

chapters.title: Capítulo 6: O cobertor de Fifi
chapters.synopsis: O cobertor de folha de Fifi voa com o vento, e os amigos fazem uma corrente para pegá-lo.
chapters.text:
Fifi, a formiga, tinha um cobertor feito de uma folha macia. Uma noite, o vento soprou e levou o cobertor para cima de uma pedra alta.
Fifi tentou subir. Sobe, sobe, e nada de chegar!
Fifi chamou Tico, o tatu. Fifi subiu nas costas de Tico. Sobe, sobe, e nada de chegar!
Tico chamou Quinha, a pata. Tico subiu nas costas de Quinha, e Fifi nas costas de Tico. Sobe, sobe, e nada de chegar!
Quinha chamou Lelé, a lebre. Lelé ficou bem embaixo, firme como uma pedra. Quinha subiu em Lelé, Tico subiu em Quinha, Fifi subiu em Tico.
Sobe, sobe... e Fifi pegou o cobertor!
A torre de amigos balançou, balançou, e todos desceram com cuidado.
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — sussurraram, porque já era tarde.
Fifi se enrolou no cobertor e dormiu sorrindo.

chapters.title: Capítulo 7: A festa de todos
chapters.synopsis: Os amigos preparam uma festa e cada um traz uma coisa, até a mesa ficar completa.
chapters.text:
Os amigos resolveram fazer uma festa para comemorar todas as aventuras.
Tico, o tatu, trouxe a mesa. Mas a mesa estava vazia. Falta, falta, e nada de festa!
Quinha, a pata, trouxe o bolo. Tico trouxe a mesa, Quinha trouxe o bolo. Falta, falta, e nada de festa!
Lelé, a lebre, trouxe a pipa vermelha para enfeitar. Tico trouxe a mesa, Quinha trouxe o bolo, Lelé trouxe a pipa. Falta, falta, e nada de festa!
Então chegou Fifi, a formiga, carregando uma coisa pequenininha.
— O que é isso? — perguntaram.
— É um convite. Faltava chamar todo mundo da floresta!
Fifi entregou os convites, e logo chegaram passarinhos, sapos e borboletas.
Agora sim, a festa estava completa!
— Um puxa, dois puxam, todos juntos: conseguimos! — cantaram todos juntos.
E dançaram até as estrelas aparecerem no céu.

books.title: Pip's Guessing Garden
books.premise: Pip the mouse and her garden friends meet a new mystery each day and use clues like covers, titles, labels and footprints to predict what will happen, then check if they were right.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Big Red Boot
chapters.synopsis: Pip the mouse finds a big red boot in the garden and guesses what it could be. Inside, she finds a cosy surprise.
chapters.text:
Pip was a small grey mouse. She lived under the garden shed.
One morning, Pip saw something new on the grass. It was big. It was red. It had a long lace.
"What can it be?" said Pip. "Is it a red boat? Is it a red house?"
Pip looked at it from the front. She looked at it from the back. It was a boot! A big red boot.
"I think a giant lost it," said Pip.
Her friend Tob the frog hopped over. "I think it is a boot for a farmer," said Tob.
Pip climbed inside the boot. It was dark and soft and warm.
"Oh!" said Pip. "This boot is not for a giant. And it is not for a farmer. This boot is for me!"
Pip brought a leaf for a bed and a nut for a snack.
That night, Pip slept in the big red boot. It was the cosiest house in the whole garden.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Hole in the Hedge
chapters.synopsis: Pip and Tob guess what lives behind a hole in the hedge. It turns out to be a friendly hedgehog.
chapters.text:
Next to the garden there was a tall green hedge. At the bottom of the hedge was a round hole.
"Look, Tob," said Pip. "Who lives in there?"
Tob looked at the hole. "It is a big hole. I think a fox lives there!"
Pip was not so sure. She saw some leaves by the hole. She saw small footprints in the mud.
"The footprints are small," said Pip. "I think a small animal lives there."
They heard a sniff, sniff, sniff.
Out came a nose. Then two little eyes. Then lots and lots of spikes!
"Hello," said a sleepy voice. "I am Hettie the hedgehog. Who are you?"
"I am Pip, and this is Tob," said Pip. "We were guessing who lived here."
Hettie smiled. "Did you guess right?"
"I did!" said Pip. "The small footprints told me."
Hettie gave them a crunchy apple to share. Now they had three friends in the garden.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Book with the Moon
chapters.synopsis: Pip finds a picture book with a moon on the cover and guesses what the story is about. She checks her guess as Hettie reads it.
chapters.text:
One day, Pip found a little book under the bench. On the cover there was a big yellow moon and a small brown owl.
The title said: The Owl Who Could Not Sleep.
"I can guess this story," said Pip. "The owl is awake all night and it cannot sleep in the day."
"Let us find out," said Hettie. She opened the book and began to read.
In the story, the owl was called Olu. In the day, the sun was too bright. The birds sang too loudly. Olu could not sleep at all!
"My guess was right!" said Pip.
Then Olu found a dark, quiet hole in an old tree. He closed his eyes. At last, he was asleep.
"I did not guess that part," said Pip. "But I like it."
Tob yawned. "Now I want to sleep too," he said.
And all three friends had a little nap in the shade.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Splash in the Pond
chapters.synopsis: Pip hears a big splash and guesses what made it. The answer is a surprise from the sky.
chapters.text:
Pip and Tob were sitting by the pond. The water was still and shiny.
SPLASH! Big drops of water flew everywhere.
"What was that?" cried Pip. "I think a big fish jumped!"
"I think a stone fell in," said Tob.
They looked at the water. Little rings went round and round.
Then something white popped up. It had a long neck and an orange beak.
"It is not a fish," said Pip. "And it is not a stone."
"Hello!" said the white bird. "I am Dot the duck. Sorry for the big splash. I landed too fast!"
Pip laughed. "We had two guesses, and both were wrong!"
"That is fine," said Dot. "Guessing is fun, and now you know."
Dot gave Pip and Tob a ride across the pond on her back.
"Next time I hear a splash," said Pip, "I will look up at the sky too!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Box with Holes
chapters.synopsis: Pip finds a box with holes and a label. She uses the clues to guess what is inside before she opens it.
chapters.text:
On the garden path there was a brown box. The box had small holes on the top.
On the side was a label. It said: Seeds. Plant me!
"What is inside?" asked Tob. "Is it a toy?"
Pip looked at the label. "The label says seeds," she said. "I think there are seeds inside."
"Why are there holes?" asked Hettie.
"Hmm," said Pip. "Maybe the seeds need air."
They opened the box. Inside were lots of little black seeds and a picture of a tall yellow flower.
"Sunflowers!" said Dot. "They grow very tall."
The friends dug a row of small holes in the soil. They put one seed in each hole. Tob gave them some water from the pond.
"Now we wait," said Pip.
"How long?" asked Tob.
"Many days," said Dot.
Tob sighed. Waiting is the hardest part!

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The Shadow on the Wall
chapters.synopsis: Pip sees a scary shadow on the shed wall and guesses it is a monster. It turns out to be something small and friendly.
chapters.text:
It was evening. The sun was low and orange.
Pip saw a huge shadow on the wall of the shed. It had long legs and big round ears.
"Help!" squeaked Pip. "It is a monster!"
Tob hid behind a flowerpot. Hettie rolled into a spiky ball.
But Dot did not hide. "Look at the shadow carefully," she said. "What makes shadows?"
"The sun," said Pip. "When something is in front of the light."
Pip turned round. There, on a stone, sat a tiny brown rabbit. The low sun made its shadow very, very big!
"Hello," said the rabbit. "I am Bina. Why is everyone hiding?"
Everyone laughed, even Hettie.
"We thought you were a monster," said Pip. "But you are only small."
"Small, but brave," said Bina, and she hopped over to say hello.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Tall Yellow Surprise
chapters.synopsis: After many days, the friends guess what the green shoots will become. They throw a party under the tall sunflowers.
chapters.text:
Many days went by. Little green shoots came up out of the soil.
"What will they be?" asked Bina. She was new, so she did not know.
"Remember the picture on the box?" said Pip. "I predict they will be tall and yellow."
Every day, the shoots grew a bit taller. They grew taller than Pip. They grew taller than Tob. They grew taller than Dot!
One sunny morning, the friends woke up and gasped. Big yellow flowers looked down at them like happy faces.
"Sunflowers!" shouted Bina. "Pip, your prediction was right!"
"The clues helped me," said Pip. "The picture, the label and the seeds."
The friends had a party under the sunflowers. Hettie brought apples. Dot brought pond water. Bina brought a carrot.
Pip brought her big red boot, full of seeds to share.
"What a garden," said Tob. "I wonder what we will find tomorrow!"
